problems.title: The forward Brownian identity omits a Laplacian drift
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v 3, Appendix A.2, Eq.(17), PDF p.17; Appendix B, Eq.(35), p.20
claim: For forward Brownian motion \(dX_t=dW_t\), Eq.(17) writes \[U(X_0,0)=U(X_T,T)-\int_0^T\nabla U\cdot dW_t+\tfrac12\int_0^T\|\nabla U\|^2dt.\]
analysis:
For the true heat-flow energy \(U=-\log p_t\), \(\partial_tU=	frac12\Delta U-	frac12\|
abla U\|^2\). Forward Itô calculus therefore gives \[dU=
abla U\cdot dW_t+(\Delta U-	frac12\|
abla U\|^2)dt.\] Take the normalized heat flow \(p_t=\mathcal N(0,1+t)\). Then \(U(y,t)=	frac12\log[2\pi(1+t)]+y^2/[2(1+t)]\) and \(\Delta U=1/(1+t)\). The printed right-hand side exceeds the true initial energy by \(\log(1+T)\) on every Brownian path, almost surely. At \(T=1\), the gap is \(\log2>0\).

A right-endpoint stochastic integral adds the quadratic-covariation term \(\int\Delta U\,dt\), so that convention can rescue the displayed formula. It is not the ordinary forward Itô reading of the stated forward SDE. This is a background estimator identity; the spatial/time-score training objectives do not use this formula.
result: The stated forward interpretation needs a drift correction or an explicit backward-integral convention. This does not establish an error in the reported learned-energy likelihood measurements.
problems.impact_rationale: The false forward identity is confined to a background estimator derivation; the central dual-score training identities remain intact.
repair: For a smooth true heat-flow energy, subtract \(\int_0^T\Delta U(X_t,t)dt\) from the printed right-hand side. Alternatively, explicitly define and consistently discretize a right-endpoint integral.
assumptions: The density is positive and smooth; the stochastic integral uses the forward Itô convention.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing correction is retained as a bounded proposal; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Bayes optimality does not give a pointwise dimensionality upper bound
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v 3, Eq.(11), PDF p.9; Appendix C.3, p.22
claim: Appendix C.3 claims the denoiser-MSE dimensionality estimate upper-bounds the true dimensionality. Equation (11) conditions on an individual clean image \(X=x\).
analysis: Let the true clean law be \(P=\mathcal N(0,1)\), noise variance \(t=1\), and model law \(Q=\mathcal N(0,1/3)\). Both give smooth, normalized heat flows. The true denoiser is \(m(y)=y/2\), while the model-energy denoiser is \(g(y)=y/4\). With \(Y=x+Z\) and \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), \[D(x,1)=(x^2+1)/4,\qquad D_g(x,1)=(9x^2+1)/16.\] Thus \(D_g-D=(5x^2-3)/16<0\) throughout \(|x|<\sqrt{3/5}\), a set of positive probability. At \(x=0\), the estimate is \(1/16\) versus the true \(1/4\).

Bayes orthogonality instead gives the population identity \[\mathbb E\|X-g(Y)\|^2=\mathbb E\|X-m(Y)\|^2+\mathbb E\|m(Y)-g(Y)\|^2.\] Its cross term vanishes after conditioning on \(Y\), not after fixing \(X=x\). In this same example, population dimensionalities are \(1/2\) and \(5/8\), so population Bayes optimality survives.
result: The one-sided interpretation of individual-image dimensionalities is invalid. Their actual observed curves, nonnegativity and the population MSE bound are not disproved.
problems.impact_rationale: The defect changes a confidence interpretation of individual dimensionality curves, without refuting the dual-score method or establishing numerical errors in those curves.
repair: State the upper bound only after averaging over the true clean-data law: \(\mathbb E_XD_g=\mathbb E_XD+t^{-1}\mathbb E\|m_t(Y)-g_t(Y)\|^2\). Individual-image estimates remain nonnegative but have no general one-sided error guarantee.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing correction is retained as a bounded proposal; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: The homogeneity discussion depends on regularity at the origin
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v 3, Appendix B.2, PDF p.19
claim: The discussion relates a conservative degree-one homogeneous score to Gaussian conditionals along affine lines.
analysis: Degree-one homogeneity with differentiability at the origin implies \(s(y)=Ds(0)y\), by evaluating \([s(hy)-s(0)]/h\) as \(h\downarrow0\). Conservativity then gives a symmetric quadratic potential; normalizability requires a positive-definite precision. Gaussian conditionals follow. A counterexample based on \(V(a,b)=\tfrac12\sqrt{a^4+b^4}\) lacks score differentiability at the origin and therefore does not refute this globally differentiable reading.
result: Retain this as a regularity clarification. No separate error is established under the stronger smoothness interpretation, and no exact Gaussian claim is inferred for the approximately homogeneous trained architecture.
problems.impact_rationale: The proposed counterexample violates the origin differentiability that rescues the relevant implication.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper repair is asserted for this scoped finding.
